title: Class-Conditional Distribution Balancing for Group Robust Classification
claim: Reweighting toward minority groups rebalances class-conditional distributions, yielding a decision boundary that ignores spurious features whether they are correlated, independent, or entangled.
layout: 4 panels: causal graph left, three 2-D scatter panels right, shared legend
description: The left panel is a causal graph. A dashed node u points to latent nodes z_c and z_s, which point to the grey observed nodes y and x. A green legend box defines dashed, grey and white nodes. To the right, a legend bar explains the decision boundaries of ERM, stable learning and CCDB, the dataset center, and class centers before and after reweighting. Three toy 2-D scatter panels (a, b, c) show blue and red class clusters inside rounded capsule outlines. Yellow glows mark up-weighted points and blue glows mark down-weighted points. Yellow dashed arrows run from the original class means μ1 and μ2 to the reweighted means. Red, grey and green dashed lines show how the decision boundaries differ across the three correlation settings.
caption: Left: Causal graph. Right: Analyzing the effectiveness of our method under three extreme configurations where $\zv_{\ts}$ and $y$ are: (a) strongly correlated with well-disentangled predefined features; (b) completely independent; and (c) strongly correlated with predefined features that are independent but semantically entangled. Each case consists of two classes (marked in blue and red). Data points in the yellow regions are assigned with high weights, while those in the blue regions are assigned with low weights.
abstract: Spurious correlations that lead models to correct predictions for the wrong reasons pose a critical challenge for robust real-world generalization. Existing research attributes this issue to group imbalance and addresses it by maximizing group-balanced or worst-group accuracy, which heavily relies on expensive bias annotations. A compromise approach involves predicting bias information using extensively pretrained foundation models, which requires large-scale data and becomes impractical for resource-limited rare domains. To address these challenges, we offer a novel perspective by reframing the spurious correlations as imbalances or mismatches in class-conditional distributions, and propose a simple yet effective robust learning method that eliminates the need for both bias annotations and predictions. With the goal of maximizing the conditional entropy (uncertainty) of the label given spurious factors, our method leverages a sample reweighting strategy to achieve class-conditional distribution balancing, which automatically highlights minority groups and classes, effectively dismantling spurious correlations and producing a debiased data distribution for classification. Extensive experiments and analysis demonstrate that our approach consistently delivers state-of-the-art performance, rivaling methods that rely on bias supervision.
